extracted.intended_audience: PTO management, oversight bodies (OMB, Congress), auditors, and stakeholders (inventors, practitioners, public)
extracted.subtask_description: Annual report material (FY1999) describing the PTO's GPRA performance goals and measures across Patents, Trademarks, Information Dissemination, and Policy areas, together with independent auditor criteria/observations and summaries of controlling litigation affecting patent practice. Useful for evaluating agency performance, compliance, and relevant legal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit standards and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The audit was conducted in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards (GAAS), Government Auditing Standards, and OMB Bulletin 98-08, Audit Requirements for Federal Financial Statements, as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These standards require planning and performing the audit to obtain reasonable assurance whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement; include examining on a test basis evidence supporting amounts and disclosures; assessing accounting principles used and significant estimates; and evaluating overall financial statement presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditor's opinion on financial statements (fair presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements should present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The auditor's expressed opinion (unqualified) is the criterion that the consolidated balance sheet and related statements conform materially to GAAP for the fiscal year audited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit objective — reasonable assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the audit is to obtain reasonable (not absolute) assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit includes tests of evidence, controls, estimates, and presentation; inherent limitations mean material misstatements may nonetheless occur undetected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal control objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal control should provide management reasonable assurance that assets are safeguarded; transactions are executed in accordance with management's authorization and recorded properly for GAAP; and data supporting reported performance measures are properly recorded and accounted for to permit preparation of reliable and complete performance information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of inherent limitations, controls provide reasonable not absolute assurance; design/operation may deteriorate or become inadequate as conditions change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal control testing scope limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The auditors limited internal control testing to controls necessary to achieve objectives described in OMB Bulletin 98-08 and did not test all internal controls relevant to operating objectives as defined by the Federal Managers' Financial Integrity Act of 1982.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The audit's objective was not to provide blanket assurance on internal control; therefore no opinion on internal control was provided and some deficiencies relevant to operational efficiency may not be detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reportable conditions and material weaknesses (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reportable conditions are significant deficiencies in the design or operation of internal control that could adversely affect an entity's ability to record/process/report financial data consistent with management's assertions. Material weaknesses are reportable conditions where the risk of material misstatement is not reduced to a relatively low level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditors note/report these matters when identified; absence of noted material weaknesses was reported for the PTO in FY1999.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance testing and scope (laws/regulations & FFMIA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors perform tests of compliance with certain provisions of laws and regulations that could have a direct and material effect on financial statements and with requirements referred to in OMB Bulletin 98-08, including requirements of the Federal Financial Management Improvement Act (FFMIA) of 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests are limited to specified provisions; providing an opinion on compliance with all laws/regulations is not an objective of the financial statement audit; noncompliance may occur and not be detected by the tests performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial management systems substantial compliance (FFMIA implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial management systems should substantially comply with federal financial management systems requirements, applicable accounting standards, and the U.S. Standard General Ledger at the transaction level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Auditor's tests (using Appendix D implementation guidance of OMB Bulletin 98-08) found no instances of non-substantial compliance for the PTO in FY1999.

rubrics_metrics.name: GPRA requirement (agency strategic goals & measurement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under GPRA, federal agencies must establish strategic goals, measure their performance, and report on how well they have met goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTO developed a performance measurement system to support mission/strategy, focus on customers, and provide measures for continuous improvement; tables summarize GPRA goals, measures, and indicators for major business areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Business Area — Performance Goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance Goal: Grant exclusive rights, for limited times, to inventors for their discoveries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This overarching goal is assessed via multiple effectiveness, customer/employee satisfaction, productivity, efficiency, quantity, and quality measures described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Business Area — Effectiveness measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectiveness Measures include number of original inventions filed and number of UPR applications filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baselines, targets, and actuals are tracked year-to-year (examples: original inventions filed, UPR application counts). Note: 'original inventions' exclude certain continuations and requests for continuing prosecution per footnote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Business Area — Customer satisfaction measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall percentage of customer satisfaction (measured via survey).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline, target, and actual percentages are tracked annually (e.g., baseline 50%, target 65%, actual 57% for FY1999). Surveys not always performed every year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Business Area — Employee satisfaction measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall percentage of employee satisfaction measured from a culture survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline and targets are tracked (e.g., baseline 41%, FY1999 target 75%). Survey frequency/coverage affects comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Business Area — Productivity measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of weighted applications disposed (per examiner FTE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure examiner productivity; tracked as baseline/target/actual (e.g., baseline 87.2; FY1999 actual 91.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Business Area — Efficiency measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Workload cost indicator — unit cost of weighted applications disposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitors cost efficiency per disposed weighted application (examples of dollar amounts provided for baseline/targets/actuals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Business Area — Quantity measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of total applications (UPR) disposed per year (includes SIRs) and number of UPR patents issued per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts used to measure throughput; baselines, targets, and actuals reported annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Business Area — Quality of output (process) measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Cycle time (average months) for original inventions processed; percentage of original inventions achieving 12-month or less cycle time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitors timeliness and process quality; targets set for proportion meeting 12-month goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Business Area — Performance Goal and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance Goal: Enhance trademark protection. Measures include effectiveness (applications filed by classes), productivity (disposals per FTE), efficiency (unit cost per disposal), quality (actual pendency to first action and to disposal/registration), customer satisfaction, and employee satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets and actuals are tracked across years; pendency (months) is a key quality/timeliness indicator; efficiency measured in dollars per disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Dissemination Business Area — Performance Goal and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance Goal: Promote awareness of, and access to, patent and trademark information. Measures include timeliness (percentage of key products/services meeting schedules), efficiency (unit cost of key products), effectiveness (customer evaluation of ease of access; percentage of top 100 populated areas served by PTDLs), customer satisfaction, and employee satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores and percentages tracked with attention to changes in survey scales (note: IDO moved from a four-point to five-point scale in FY1999 affecting comparability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy Area — Performance Goal and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance Goal: Help protect, promote, and expand intellectual property rights systems throughout the United States and abroad. Effectiveness measures include number of countries provided technical assistance and number of technical assistance activities completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counts and targets reported annually (examples: baseline 47 countries; FY1999 actuals 93).

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation — standard of appellate review for PTO fact-finding (Dickinson v. Zurko)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supreme Court held that the APA standard of review ("arbitrary, capricious, abuse of discretion" / "substantial evidence" for agency fact-finding) applies to judicial review of PTO findings of fact, not the 'clearly erroneous' standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impacts how PTO factual determinations are reviewed on appeal; agencies and courts must apply APA deference standards when assessing PTO factual findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness — requirement of motivation to combine references (In re Dance & In re Dembiczak)
rubrics_metrics.description: To sustain an obviousness rejection, the PTO/Board must identify some suggestion, teaching, or motivation in the prior art to select and combine specific teachings; simplicity of prior art rarely weighs against obviousness of a more complicated device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to specifically identify motivation to combine prior art references can lead to reversal on appeal; courts will not supplement missing findings on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness-type double patenting between design and utility patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Obviousness-type double patenting between design and utility patents is possible only in very rare cases where the claims cross-read such that the subject matter of one would have been obvious from the other, and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection on this basis requires showing that design patent claims are obvious variants of the pending utility claims; mere relatedness is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement and claim interpretation standards (In re Cortright)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim interpretation by the PTO must be reasonable in view of the specification and other patents; enablement under 35 U.S.C. § 112, ¶ 1 requires adequate disclosure to support claimed scope. Overbroad readings (e.g., interpreting 'restore' to require full restoration) may be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may rely on usage/definitions of terms in other issued patents when assessing reasonableness of PTO claim interpretation; lack of evidence supporting claimed mechanisms (e.g., biochemical effect) can sustain rejections for lack of enablement.
